questions.stem: R=[[0,-1,0],[1,0,0],[0,0,1]] maps body components to fixed-frame A components, and ω_A=(2,0,0) rad/s; which Rdot is correct?
assumptions: Right-hand cross-product convention; R maps body coordinates into the fixed frame.

citations.locator: Lecture 3, physical PDF page 104, printed slide 10: relevant text, equations and associated figures
citations.evidenceText:
Calculus – Time derivatives

•  Time Derivatives of Vectors and Matrices
   – The derivative of a time-varying matrix 𝐀(𝐭) or vector 𝒙(𝑡) is defined as the
       matrix or vector composed of the derivatives of its individual elements.

                              𝑑         𝑑
               ሶ𝐀𝐭=                  𝑑𝑡𝐀𝐭= 𝑑𝑡𝑎𝑖𝑗𝑡
   – This is essential for expressing the dynamics of a rigid body where position
      and orientation are functions of time.
   – For a rotation matrix 𝐑(𝐭), the derivative is
     ሶ𝐑= 𝐒(𝝎)𝐑, where 𝐒(𝝎) is a skew-symmetric
       matrix representing angular velocity 𝝎.





                                                                                                          10

solution.justification: For fixed-frame angular-velocity components, multiply on the left: S(ω_A)R. The result is not generally skew-symmetric, even though S(ω_A)=Rdot Rᵀ is.

optionExplanations.o2: This is RS(ω_A), which uses the wrong side for fixed-frame ω_A.
optionExplanations.o3: This is S(ω_A) alone, omitting the nonidentity R.

steps: Multiply this matrix by R on the right.
The second row becomes (0,0,-2) and the third becomes (2,0,0).

assumptions: R is a differentiable proper rotation matrix.

assumptions: The same physical angular velocity is expressed in A and B; R is a proper rotation.

options.text: Rdot itself is skew-symmetric for every orientation

solution.justification: Differentiating RRᵀ=I and RᵀR=I gives the two skew matrices; their angular velocities are expressed in different frames. Rdot alone need not be skew.

optionExplanations.o1: Differentiating RRᵀ=I establishes the fixed-frame skew matrix.
optionExplanations.o2: Differentiating RᵀR=I establishes the body-frame skew matrix.
optionExplanations.o3: Only the products with R or Rᵀ are guaranteed skew; a nonidentity rotation supplies counterexamples.
optionExplanations.o4: Changing angular-velocity coordinates changes which side the skew matrix multiplies.

steps: Differentiate RRᵀ=I to obtain Rdot Rᵀ+R Rdotᵀ=0.
